jobs.prompt:
fix(cpp): return freed heap to the system so the gateway's memory stops growing under real traffic

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`), C++ only (do NOT install or run Bun, Node, Deno, Rust or Cargo). Read `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release|asan <test>`), `docs/RUNTIME.md`, `src/rt/memory.cpp` + `include/uos/rt/memory.hpp` (the `/health` `memory` object: resident, anonymous, allocator in-use/free/mmap, per-cache entries and bytes), the memory findings under `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/` (cppgw-memory-*), and the benchmark those findings describe (a synthetic upstream with programmed replies driven by the real Codex CLI). Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body (short, plain language).

EVIDENCE FROM THE DEPLOYED GATEWAY (Linux ARM64, glibc, one process, about two hours of real Codex client traffic: `/v1/models` catalog fetches of 70-390 kB, streamed `/v1/responses` turns with request bodies up to several hundred kB, SQLite KV reads/writes):
- at start: resident 26 MiB, anonymous 3.8 MiB, allocator in-use 2.4 MiB, allocator free 2.7 MiB
- after 4 requests: resident 42.7, anonymous 10.2, in-use 5.3, free 7.5
- after ~25 min: resident 50.7, anonymous 18.2, in-use 8.0, free 12.8
- after ~2 h: resident 75.2, anonymous 42.5, in-use 7.7, free 37.1, allocator mmap 0
- every tracked cache stays under about 2 MiB (sqlite_pages 2.0 MiB, codex_catalog 1.8 MiB).
So live data is flat at about 8 MiB while memory the allocator has freed but keeps (it never goes back to the kernel) grows without bound seen so far. The goal host class has 464 MiB of RAM in total, so this matters.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner, Ubuntu 26.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network. `sudo apt-get install -y clang ninja-build pkg-config ccache libboost-json-dev libboost-container-dev libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev`; the CI workflow shows the exact list and how it builds the pinned SQLite.

RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Tests use local mocks only: no real provider traffic.
- Your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed: commit after each step and keep a checklist in `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-memory-3-allocator-20261122.md`. Work in small steps. No foreground command longer than about 10 minutes.
- Do not delete or weaken tests. No behaviour change visible to clients.

TASK
1. Reproduce first. Extend the existing memory benchmark (or add a focused one) so it shows the same signature on this runner: allocator in-use flat, allocator free growing across many rounds of mixed large and small requests on several concurrent connections. Find out WHY the freed memory is retained: which threads allocate (count the process's threads and glibc arenas: `malloc_info`, `mallinfo2`, `/proc/self/smaps`), whether the retained memory is fragmented top-of-heap, per-thread arenas, or large blocks below the mmap threshold (glibc raises its dynamic mmap threshold after freeing large blocks, after which large buffers come from the heap and are not returned). Write the measured cause into the findings file before fixing.
2. Fix the cause with the smallest robust change, and measure each candidate rather than assuming: for example fixed `mallopt` settings at startup (M_MMAP_THRESHOLD / M_TRIM_THRESHOLD / M_ARENA_MAX, which also disable the dynamic threshold), a rate-limited `malloc_trim` when the process goes idle or after large buffers are released, reusing or shrinking the large transient buffers at their source (body/JSON/SSE/catalog buffers) so they are not repeatedly allocated at different sizes, or a combination. Do not add a third-party allocator unless the measurements show the glibc options cannot reach the target; if you conclude that, say so with numbers and stop short of vendoring one. The fix must work in the sealed, Landlock+seccomp-confined process (check the syscalls it needs, e.g. madvise/munmap/brk, are permitted by the existing seccomp policy; do not widen the policy beyond what is needed and document any addition) and must not depend on environment variables set by the operator.
3. Target: after the benchmark's traffic stops, anonymous memory returns to within about 6 MiB of live data, and across at least 20 rounds allocator free stays bounded (no upward trend). Throughput and latency of the benchmark must not regress by more than a few percent; report before/after numbers for memory, throughput and CPU.
4. Add a regression test that runs in CI in bounded time (release config) and fails if retained free heap after a burst of large requests exceeds a generous fixed bound; keep it robust on loaded runners (measure bytes, not time). Keep `/health` memory fields as they are; you may add fields (e.g. arena count, last trim) if useful.
5. Run the affected suites in release and `--config asan` (the fix must be inert or safe under sanitizers), and document the change in `docs/RUNTIME.md`.

DONE WHEN
The benchmark shows retained free heap bounded and returned after load, with numbers in the findings file, a CI regression test guards it, and existing tests pass unchanged.
